summary: SL-091 made 'Show in Explorer' refuse instead of falsely reporting Exact. For a Hidden, non-volume-root target, ShellReveal.Walk reads Explorer's view once through read-only SHGetSetSettings(0x00040001). If that view hides the item, Walk returns Failed/HiddenByExplorerSettings, never calls the open, and the status line names the Folder Options label. Around that sit a hide-only test override, a hook failpoint that fails closed before Main, the R-003 window case, the NoExplorerViewMember mutant, two twinned src rules and a 63-row write-guard corpus. It followed Q-175 (refuse, open nothing), not the brief's 'parent-only' wording. It shipped after 2 build-checks, 4 risk-spike runs, 2 designs, 4 critiques, 3 code reviews and 4 validations, with O-041 (is the cached settings read stale in a running app) carried to SC-162. Explorer's real selection at Hidden=2 was not re-measured through the new build.

payload.reason: Reflection written from the slice record. Nothing blocked it. The Hidden=2 behaviour of Explorer itself was never observed through this build, and that is recorded as an unknown, not a finding.

learned.lesson: Do not let a blocked Hidden=2 spike become an 'assumed' line that a design builds on. Two sources answer Hidden=2 questions without asking the owner to change Explorer's settings: (1) Windows Sandbox, which defaults to Hidden=2, and where the real ShellReveal.cs compiled into a harness ran unattended; (2) engine.db's stored runs, which hold run 2285's full results-Defaults.json and its run.ps1 as run 2244's events. The same read-only harness trick, a private HKCU hive loaded in the harness process only, decoded bit 15 (O-042) without touching the owner's settings. Try both before design. Their limits are build 26100 against the host's 26200, an elevated (High-integrity) Explorer, 8.3 names off, and LongPathsEnabled=0 until bootstrapped.
learned.evidence: risk-spike #2 passed 'built anyway' with assumption (3), that a hidden ancestor does not block selection. That assumption became fork O-017, which forced a re-synthesis AFTER design #1 had passed critique #2. Risk-spike #3 then settled it: Sandbox 18/18 per +H and +H+S ancestor class with 12/12 control rounds, and run 2285's control read from the engine DB under +H AppData. Design #2 and critique #3/#4 followed. O-042 was discharged with the private hive in validate.

learned.lesson: A follow-up row that cites a Q-id must have that answer folded in before the survey derives criteria. The brief and derived C2-C4 said 'parent-only, and say so'. Q-175 (human) said refuse, open nothing, name the setting. The designer had to restate C2-C4 in key_decisions ('validate should read C2-C4 as not reported as landing, setting named, nothing opened'), and validate had to read the criteria through that note. Any check written against the brief's wording for this slice would pass for the wrong reason.
learned.evidence: Build-check criteria C2-C4 ('parent-only') against design key_decisions[0] and Q-175. Q-169 also says 'says it opened the parent folder'; the design records that Q-175 supersedes it.

learned.lesson: A design invariant marked must-verify whose only proof needs the owner to toggle Explorer's settings becomes a validate-aimed obligation. Validate cannot discharge it, so it burns laps. Mark it person-owned in filed_for_later when the design is written. The one dischargeable must-verify (bit 15, O-042) was cheap with a private hive. The unfixable one (O-041, does Explorer's Apply clear shell32's per-process cached view) is not.
learned.evidence: validate-slice #1 halted on O-041 and O-042. #2 and #3 halted on O-041 alone. Attempt 3 re-ran the full suite, mutants and harness. The loop waived O-041 to SC-162 at 01:24Z and #4 passed with no new work. Attempt 2 had already measured that a raw registry change went unseen for at least 3.8 s. Attempt 3 did not try the Sandbox route the 01:03Z decision asked for, and did not say why.

learned.lesson: Walk now refuses every Hidden target the view hides BEFORE the open (ShellReveal.cs:318-323). Anything that compiles live src ShellReveal.cs or drives the shipped exe can no longer observe Explorer's own selection at those settings. That covers spike-92's X1 row, R-001 step 5 and R-003(d). Any future 'what does Explorer select at (h,s)' measurement needs a gate-bypassing harness: Walk with an explorer delegate returning ExplorerView(true,true), or spike-74's run.ps1, which calls SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems itself. A slice that changes Walk's gate must ask, for each filed person-run, whether it still reaches the open.
learned.evidence: Code-review round 2 finding R2-m2 (carried to SC-159). The design's filed_for_later item 1 and its reuse of the spike-92 harness both assumed the exe or RevealAsync still reached the open.

learned.lesson: Engine-appended architecture_rules persist in the working tree across design attempts. A same-named rule from a taken-back attempt is not replaced, and the new design's rule B was silently skipped. The survey of HEAD (36b461d) did not show this, so design #1 planned against a fitness.yaml that did not match the tree. Build had to reset .taad/fitness.yaml to HEAD's 1086 lines and hand-write rules A and B above the first '# settled by SL-' marker. The twinned rules were also renamed to Fact-style names. A re-design would make the engine append settled copies of A and B, which STRAY-HIT plants F41-F48 and move the settled count of 63. Re-read the working tree, not HEAD, after any take-back.
learned.evidence: critique review n1 (.taad/fitness.yaml:1088-1142 attempt-1 block, :1144-1176 A and C only); build O-043; code-review drift at .taad/fitness.yaml:267-286 ('OnlyShellRevealReadsOrOverridesExplorersViewSettings (*.cs)', 'TheAppNeverWritesExplorersSettings (*.cs)').

learned.lesson: Window cases behave differently under the engine's TEMP (C:\WINDOWS\TEMP) than under the owner's (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp): the root is 18 characters shorter. B-008's check 'title and detail run longer than a system drive's' fails at 384 against 400 characters. Validate marked B-008 not-run even though this slice re-pinned its status text (WindowCases.ps1:4360). Window runs for a slice that touches B-007/B-008 should either pad the root to a fixed length, as R-001 does, or expect that one failure. Pointing TEMP at the user temp to get green made the guard later name those folders as the repo and C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
learned.evidence: build: B-008 failed only on that check under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and passed under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. S-001 passed at 560x644. validate-slice: B-008 not-run.

learned.lesson: Line references the design carries over from earlier slices' lessons are unreliable for tests/window/**. Survey must measure them before design. Two sets were wrong. The StartupHook.cs ':197-200 and :278' were the stopping-log fields and the end of ArmFailListing, not the mode check. The hs_file.sys pin cited as R-002's is in Test-R001 (:3649, step at :3775-3782), and Test-R002 starts at :4213. Critique caught both, but a builder acting on them would have edited the wrong case.
learned.evidence: critique findings m6 and n5. The design's coherence_check itself says StartupHook.cs, RevealMode.cs and MainWindow.xaml line refs were 'carried as the designer's', not measured.

learned.lesson: Sizing of medium with medium risk was right on risk but low on effort. Half of the laps came from access to a measurement (Hidden=2), not from the code. Walk's gate is about 60 lines. The size was in the guard and plumbing: 13 files across Core, App, hook, window cases, mutants, fitness.yaml, plants.json and a 63-row corpus, plus a hook variable, a mutant and pins that must be added in several places (WindowMutants.ps1 still hard-codes its -Mutant All roster beside the ValidateSet because Q-115's startup check is unbuilt). Open a slice that adds a hook variable or a write-guard rule as larger than its production diff suggests.
learned.evidence: Rework counts: build-check 2, risk-spike 4, design 2, critique 4, code-review 3 (one refused, one halted on drift), validate 4. Build deviations list, including the wider rule B and C patterns and the closed-as-a-class corpus.

missed.what: The design's person sitting and its harness reuse could not do what they said. filed_for_later item 1 had the owner 're-measure 0/13 through the shipped exe', and 'whats_reused' named the spike-92 harness, which compiles the live ShellReveal.cs. The same design's gate refuses every hidden target before the open, so neither could observe Explorer's selection. The check was missing: for each filed measurement, name the code path that still reaches SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems after the gate. Four critique passes did not ask it.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2, as finding R2-m2 (carried to SC-159)

missed.what: The design's Walk contract lists 'An open failure after a visible verdict gives Failed / None with that hr', but its 14-row case matrix has no row for it. The only open-failure test walks the never-created C:\a\b.txt, so its attribute read throws and the Hidden-visible open-failure branch is never reached. The build then changed what that branch carries (Hidden, System and View), and a regression there would have stayed green. Every error_case in a contract needs a case row or an explicit 'immaterial' entry.
missed.caught_by: code-review, as finding x1 (carried to SC-157)

missed.what: The design listed mid-session freshness of SHGetSetSettings both as a cross-domain invariant marked 'must-verify' and as a filed person item. The invariant became validate-aimed obligation O-041, which needs a person to toggle Explorer's settings. The critique did not force a single owner for it, so validate ran three laps on an obligation it could not discharge.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice attempts 1-3 halting on O-041, then the loop's waiver to SC-162

what_went_wrong: Design #1 passed critique #2 with the ancestor question (O-017) still open and flagged as forcing a re-synthesis. The spike that settled it (risk-spike #3) came afterwards, so design #1 was rewritten as design #2 and critiqued again (critique #3/#4, 5 more findings). Risk-spike #1 had halted on exactly the Hidden=2 access problem and risk-spike #2 passed it as an assumption. The stored-run read and the Sandbox route that later settled it were available then.

The brief's 'parent-only' wording contradicted Q-175's 'refuse, open nothing'. Build-check derived C2-C4 from the brief, so the survey reported them as missing in a form the product deliberately does not satisfy. Design had to reinterpret them in key_decisions, and validate had to read them through that note.

Build-check ran twice. The first run halted because its reply reported C5 as present but said 'unbuilt', so the engine read the verdict as partial and asked a person. The second run passed 'built anyway' with no new information.

The design's fitness.yaml plan was written against a survey of HEAD (36b461d). The tree held attempt 1's leftover SL-091 block (:1088-1142). The engine skipped the same-named rule B, so it was never appended. Critique n1 caught it. Build reset fitness.yaml to HEAD and hand-wrote the rules.

The builder re-pointed TEMP to the owner's user temp to get B-008, S-006, R-003 and B-007 green. The guard later named those folders as the repo and C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. The cases cleaned up and a check found nothing left, but B-008 under the engine's own TEMP was never shown green and validate left it not-run.

Code review ran three times. #1 was refused (provider turn-away). #2 halted on two undeclared departures (twinned rules renamed Fact-style) plus the finding that the owner's sitting could not measure what it claimed. Only #3 passed, and all of its 3 findings were disposed by a model.

Validate ran four times. Three laps re-ran the full suite, the window mutants and the rules harness while O-041 (needs a person to toggle Explorer's settings) stayed open. #4 passed with no new work once the loop waived O-041 to SC-162. Attempt 3 skipped the Sandbox route a 01:03Z decision asked for and recorded no reason.

The slice ships without anyone observing Explorer's real selection through the new build. R-001 step 5 and R-002 (person-run landings) were not executed. 0/13 at Hidden=2 remains the owner's single hand run. The (1,1) cell is predicted from a private-hive decode only. All 25 critique findings (10 plus 15) and the 3 code-review findings were answered by a model and counted as untriaged.
payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium size and medium risk, sized by a person. The risk tier was right: ShellReveal is the file Q-175 said not to cut at low tier. The size was too small. Walk's gate is small, but the slice touched 13 files and ran 2 designs, 4 critiques, 4 risk-spike runs, 3 code reviews and 4 validations. Two things drove that: the Hidden=2 measurement could not be taken without a person or the Sandbox, and the write-guard rules were closed 'as a class' with a 63-row corpus, parity and plants. The risk that cost the most was access to a measurement, not the code.
unknowns: Does shell32's cached SHGetSetSettings in a running app refresh after Explorer's own Apply or a View toggle (O-041, SC-162)? Attempt 2 saw a raw registry change go unseen for at least 3.8 s. If it is stale, the app refuses items Explorer would now show, or reports landings it will not make, until restart.

At (Hidden=1, ShowSuperHidden=1), does Explorer select a Hidden+System item on the host (26200, Medium-integrity Explorer)? The predicate returns Exact there. Only the SHGetSetSettings decode was measured, through a private hive. Explorer's selection was not. This is the only cell where the predicate claims Exact without a measurement.

Do +H direct-parent and +H+S ancestor rows hold on the host (build 26200, Medium-integrity Explorer) at Hidden=2? Evidence so far is Sandbox build 26100 with a High-integrity Explorer (18/18 per class) plus run 2285's control under +H AppData four levels up.

Can a Windows Sandbox guest's Explorer be switched between settings cells unattended (guest HKCU write plus a shell-state broadcast, or UI automation) so that its running Explorer actually follows the change? That decides whether the candidate below can replace the owner's sitting.
Windows 10: does SHGetSetSettings decode bit 0 and bit 15 the same way, and does Explorer filter hidden items the same way (Q-197, Q-199)? Nothing has been measured there.

candidates.title: Measure the Explorer view-settings cells in Windows Sandbox so the owner's Hidden=2 sitting is not the only route
candidates.why: docs/design/SL-091-hidden-reveal-refuses.md lists three measurements that wait on the owner changing Explorer's settings, and its predicate table marks (1,1) and (2,1) as predicted. The measurements are the 0/13 re-measurement through a gate-bypassing harness, the (1,1)/(2,1) cells, and the mid-session toggle. Walk's gate is at src/FsAnalyser.Core/Native/ShellReveal.cs:318-323. (1,1) is the only cell where the predicate returns Exact without an Explorer measurement. Spike hidden-ancestor-selection-at-defaults-in-windows-sandbox showed the unattended route works: the real ShellReveal.cs ran in the guest at Hidden=2 / ShowSuperHidden=0. It gave 18/18 per ancestor class and 12/12 control rounds on build 26100, with a High-integrity Explorer and 8.3 names off. Spike 91 cells 1 and 2 stayed 'blocked, need a person' because nobody tried the guest. Build a harness that sets the guest's HKCU for each of the 4 cells, bypasses Walk's gate (explorer delegate returning ExplorerView(true,true)), and records SelectedItems and window folder for H-only, H+S, System-only and plain controls. Merge with SC-159 (bypass harness wording) and SC-162 (O-041, which already names the Sandbox route) if their scope overlaps. Host-build rows (26200, Medium-integrity Explorer) and Windows 10 stay person-owned.
